text.p: South Africa gained a stranglehold on the first test after routing India for a paltry 100 on Friday.

Although Gary Kirsten was dismissed cheaply for the second time, South Africa reached 31 for one at tea, 166 ahead. South African fast bowlers took full advantage of a pitch offering both pace and bounce to remove India in just 39.1 overs.

It was the third lowest test score ever compiled at Kingsmead after Australia's 75 and South Africa's 99 in the same match during the 1949-50 series. It was also India's smallest total against South Africa.
Allan Donald took five for 40 -- his seventh five-wicket haul at test level. -- while Shaun Pollock returned figures of 2-18 and all-rounder Brian McMillan 2-27.
No Indian batsman reached 20 and their lower order collapsed tamely after lunch to lose five wickets in 12.1 overs, three departing off successive deliveries.
In the third over after the interval, Brian McMillan captured the wicket of Rahul Dravid for seven.

Donald then claimed two more wickets with the next two balls. Mongia edged to wicketkeeper Dave Richardson on four and Javagal Srinath, trying to fend off a lifting delivery, was brilliantly caught by a diving Daryll Cullinan at first slip.
David Johnson was unfortunate to be given out by New Zealand umpire Steve Dunne after a rearing Donald bumper had struck him on the shoulder.
